A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoLOR research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on SUN397, CIFAR100, and Amazon Reviews, along with ablations and Gaussian simulations in the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablations, and Gaussian simulation results.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithm 1 retain the shared representation, multiple novelty heads, joint constrained objective, primal-dual optimization, and head selection. Corrections to function-composition notation do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image and text datasets, background-shift and no-shift settings, novel-class proportions, and Gaussian separability scenarios. The revised dataset descriptions do not establish different coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches across corresponding experiments, including DD, uPU, nnPU, BODA, ARPL, CAC, PULSE, the vision-specific comparisons with SHOT, ZOC and ANNA, and the appendix MSP/Entropy comparisons.

E3.justification: The source/target construction, preprocessing, backbone choices, training procedures, sample sizes, and evaluation metrics are retained. Appendix A.5 in v3 matches A.7 in v4, including the FPR threshold of 0.01 and candidate recall grid.

E4.justification: Joint-learning ablations, sensitivity to the FPR threshold and recall-grid range/density, novel-class-size sweeps, and synthetic separability tests are retained. Figure 4 and appendix analyses are relocated or renumbered without new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions with distinct random seeds for each novel-class identity and retain the same aggregation and standard-deviation reporting. No uncertainty estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Corresponding empirical tables and plots retain their values and findings. For example, Table 2 reports CoLOR AUPRC of 0.91±0.09, 0.33±0.14, and 0.54±0.18 on SUN397, CIFAR100, and Amazon Reviews in both versions. Appendix result tables match after renumbering.

T1.justification: v4 adds Theorems 3–4 in Appendix A.2 with materially different conditions for the central AUROC guarantee, despite labeling them restatements of Theorem 1. For example, Theorem 4 uses r_eta/r_mu ≤ sqrt(N_T,1/N_T,0) instead of 4/N, alongside a revised r_mu bound. Definition 1 also separates general background shift from the support-overlap assumption. The existing proof sketch is relocated, not newly supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about scalable constrained OSDA, identifiability under background shift, advantages over domain discrimination when novelties are rare, and empirical performance across modalities. Condensed wording does not change these core claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.6 expands v3's future-work suggestion about combining domain adaptation with CoLOR into an explicit account of robust known-class classification and novelty detection, including broad architecture-compatibility assertions. Section 4.2 also revises the interpretation of the signal-strength bounds.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability statement and repository link to the abstract. Implementation and training details, including the hyperparameter table renumbered from Table 5 to Table 7, otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Impossibility Theorems for Domain Adaptation by Ben David and colleagues and SKADA-bench by Lalou and colleagues. These support the problem framing without substantially changing the positioning against prior OSDA and PU-learning methods.

P1.justification: v4 condenses selected contribution, related-work, and dataset paragraphs; adds a roadmap and notation guide; and moves the proof sketch to Appendix A.2. Author and publication information is updated, while the overall section sequence remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as a side-by-side source/target illustration with a revised caption. v4 adds notation and keyword Tables 5–6, relocates several existing displays, and introduces publication headers. The remaining figure content and experimental table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The notation guide, revised Figure 1, roadmap, and code pointer improve accessibility. However, new Theorems 3–4 give different parameter conditions while being labeled restatements of unchanged Theorem 1, without explaining their relationship to the existing proof. This ambiguity concerns a central guarantee, making the net quality effect uncertain despite the presentation gains.
